content.thinking:
I need to plan the golem's structure carefully before writing the full file in one pass: roughly 3.2 meters tall, hunched posture, oversized fists, with a skeleton rooted at the hips extending through spine, chest, neck, head, and jaw, plus arms and legs with proper joint segments. I'm mapping out which API calls to use for joints, chains, and body parts to keep everything safe and consistent.

Now I'm working out the color palette -- dark basalt brown with cel shading, gold plating, and glowing lava orange accents -- and sketching coordinate positions for the legs, using chains of hip-knee-ankle points with named joints and tapered sweep radii for a faceted, low-poly look. I'm also laying out the spine as a curved chain running up from the hips toward the chest and neck base.

For the torso, I'm thinking through sweeping an elliptical cross-section along the spine chain, widening from the hips to a broader chest, with shoulder pauldrons made of large rock-like forms attached at the top, before continuing into the neck chain.

I'm sketching the neck as a short chain parented to the chest tip, defining a single neck joint, then placing a separate head joint parented to that neck with aim direction set forward, plus a jaw joint for later. I'm also making sure the chest reference resolves to the final joint in the spine chain so the neck can parent correctly, then starting to plan the shoulder and arm joints next.

Now I'm working out the arm skeleton: shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions on each side with long golem-proportioned limbs reaching down to fist level near the knees, forming a chain parented to the chest with a tapering sweep radius for the upper and lower arm bulk. For the hands I'm planning icosahedron or box-shaped rock fists at the wrist bone, then adding finger chains -- three fingers plus a thumb per hand, each as a short multi-joint digit chain to stay within the joint budget.

Fingers extend downward from the fist rather than curling, giving a simple "extended" rest pose, and the head gets a dark flat-shaded rock shape with crown spikes, glowing eye boxes, and a lava slit mouth positioned above the shoulders. For the feet, I'm giving each foot three single-joint toe chains built from a two-point path, and I'm sketching a reusable rock-plate helper function that generates scaled, flat-shaded icosahedron or dodecahedron geometry for the body's armor plating.

Now I'm figuring out how to render lava seams across the body -- either as separate glowing rods placed along the surface, or baked directly into the skin via cellular noise, where thin cracks between cells get colored with a yellow-to-orange lava gradient while the rest stays basalt-toned with cel-shaded lighting.

For the gold plates, I'm thinking of extruding diamond outlines for the armor pieces, with a smaller glowing diamond core at the chest, possibly adding a spiral rune texture on a plane for extra detail.

For embers, I'm reconsidering floating small glowing octahedrons scattered near the body but keeping them low enough to avoid breaking the height bounds, looping through maybe a dozen or so ember pieces.

I'm budgeting part count around 300 total, limiting the palette to flat colors like gold, lava bright, lava dark, and basalt, then baking everything onto a single 1024 texture sheet. Now I'm setting up a helper function for generating rock-like parts, handling bone references and chains, and figuring out how to type the joint parameter so it accepts both a single joint and a chain.

Writing extrude geometry logic...

Computing the normal via a cross product, then adding spike options with configurable sides and colors. Now I'm planning body details like rock slabs around the pelvis using a scaled dodecahedron at the hips joint, considering a sweep for the hip loft shape.

I'm setting up the spine chain starting from the hips joint position with a tapering sweep radius, then scattering surface rocks across the torso using dodecahedron geometry sticks with varied scale and embed depth.

I'm extending the same rock scattering to the arms, forearms, thighs, and shins with sparser density, then adding glowing lava seams as a thin belt swept around the waist loop and planning similar glowing bands at other joints.

Now I'm designing the head: a dodecahedron skull scaled down, a brow slab, vertical lava diamond on the face, five crown spikes, and a wedge-shaped jaw piece with a glowing lava mouth slit between them.

Working out the jaw and head joint positions, placing a chin rock and glowing teeth, then tracing the spine path from torso to chest tip and defining the neck chain that connects the chest to the head joint.

Still placing joints and spikes for shoulders and arms, aiming for an overall height around 3.2 meters with crown and shoulder spikes, and building pauldron rock stacks with gold spike plates angled outward from the shoulders.

Still defining finger and thumb joint paths...

Now I'm working out the leg geometry: hip, knee, and ankle positions with tapering radii, then building a flat box slab for the foot so the bottom sits right at floor level, plus adding toe chunks at the front.

For the toes, I'm setting up a joint chain with rounded sweep geometry so each toe segment's bottom edge rests flush on the ground, and doing the same check for the ankle-to-leg connection. I'm also adding heel rocks behind the foot and defining the color palette—gold, lava, and dark tones—for the paint cracks and surface detailing.

I'm now defining a cracked-rock paint function that uses cell noise to detect seams, coloring thin gaps as hot lava and wider ones as regular lava while leaving the rest as basalt. I'm also planning separate mottled tints for small rocks and sticks so not everything has cracks, and thinking through the texel scale so the lava seams read as thin, realistic cracks rather than oversized stripes.

For materials, I want gold plates to use cel-shaded coloring and basalt to get similar toon shading via paint rather than lighting. For the chest emblem, I'm sketching an SVG diamond filled with lava-orange and a darker spiral stroke running through it.

Now I'm working out where to place that emblem on the chest: casting a ray forward from near the spine to find the front surface hit point, then positioning the plane there offset slightly along the normal, oriented using the hit's normal and axis so it sits flush against the torso.

I also need to make sure the scattered rocks on the chest don't overlap the emblem, so I'm filtering them out in a zone around the chest center using normal direction, height, and horizontal offset checks. Then I'm defining the torso's sweep radius as a function of the chain parameter to shape the body profile.

Adding spike generation along the spine...

Still writing dress helper...

For gold details, I'm planning octahedron plates placed near the forearm surface using sweep point frames to position and orient them correctly.

Now I'm planning a reusable shard function for spike placement on shoulders, forearms, and shins, then thinking through glow effects for lava seams at joints and veins on legs, deciding to skip those for now since paint can cover it. I'm sketching the head geometry next: a dodecahedron skull scaled for the bone shape, a lava diamond octahedron on the face, and small glowing boxes for the eyes positioned symmetrically near the head center.

I'm continuing to lay out the face details with brow rocks, crown spikes, cheek rocks, a jawbone box, and a glowing lava mouth gap, plus a chin spike. Then I'm thinking through ember glow octahedra scattered near the hips, skipping a ground lava puddle, adding glow cracks on the feet, and roughly tallying up the total part count across the torso, arms, thighs, and shins to estimate scale.

Now I'm shifting into actual code, setting up mirrored left/right limb loops, chaining joints from spine tip through arm to wrist and fingers, and configuring sweep-based skinning for the limbs with appropriate radii and colors.

Toes get similar simple two-point chains parented off the ankle, with legs deriving their side from x-position. For the lava belt loops, I'm computing cross-sectional planes at specific joints (hips, elbow) to cut cleanly across the bent limb sweeps and apply the glowing lava material.

I'll wrap each belt-cutting call in a try/catch so a failed loop just skips silently rather than crashing the whole build, since I can't test every joint angle. Then I'm finalizing torso radius profile, spine curve points, and writing the file with metadata like name "Lava Golem" and style "Genshin Impact" before committing.

I'm now sketching a `shard` helper function that places small octahedron-based gold plates (like a belt buckle) onto the surface at given azimuth/elevation, using the surface raycast to find hit points and embedding the shape partially into the mesh with scale and spin options.

Adding shoulder rocks and spikes...

Then I'm shaping the foot box with a slight yaw rotation while keeping the sole flat, plus heel rocks and a toe chain colored like rock.

Now I'm adding gold nail spikes at the toe tips, dressing the thigh with a sweep and a dodecahedron knee cap plus gold shard, and ringing the knee with lava belts. I'm also setting deterministic ember placement via a seeded rng, confirming the glow wrapper returns a proper Part, tuning eye glow strength to 1.6, and placing a flat glowing octahedron as the lava diamond on the face.

Positioning the diamond slit, eye boxes, and brow ridges on the skull front, then double-checking I only import what's actually used (polyline, rng, cells, paint, mottle, cel, svg, glow, and the V3 type) while confirming the surface-hit lookup returns a nullable Hit type before writing the base skin palette using mottled cel-shaded colors.

Checking the stroke width and confirming the square spiral stays within the diamond bounds at its widest point—good, it fits. Time to finalize and write it out.
